reuse.why: Extends the existing shouldFillCategory/averageToBudgetAmount in fill-rules.ts for the template, #fixed and include-hidden rules and has the new action use both, but each action still builds its own category query.

duplication.why: The same categories+groups+notes SELECT is copied into setZero, set3MonthAvg, set6MonthAvg, set12MonthAvg and setLastMonthSpending (plus getBudgetData), and the includeHiddenCategories ternary for the policy and the SQL hidden filter is repeated in each.

placement.why: The eligibility rules correctly live in fill-rules.ts, but the hidden rule is also decided in each action's SQL WHERE clause, splitting it across layers.

scope.why: Changes serve the four steps; a release note is added, nothing unrelated.

maintainability.why: Adding a fifth exclusion means touching every copied query, and the hidden rule lives both in the SQL and in shouldFillCategory, so the two can drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/budget/actions.ts set3MonthAvg, set6MonthAvg, set12MonthAvg and setLastMonthSpending filter hidden categories/groups in their own SQL (conditional on includeHiddenCategories) in addition to the hiddenPolicy passed to shouldFillCategory

disguised_duplication.where: the hidden rule is re-expressed as a templated SQL WHERE fragment `${includeHiddenCategories ? '' : 'AND c.hidden = 0 AND g.hidden = 0'}` beside the equivalent hiddenPolicy check in fill-rules.ts

abstraction_drift.where: fill-rules.ts gains an 'include-hidden' policy value (replacing 'include') and goal_def/group_notes inputs; set3/6/12MonthAvg and setLastMonthSpending keep deciding hidden in SQL; every action re-derives the policy from includeHiddenCategories with its own ternary
